title: Browsers and Search Engines
description: Chrome, Safari, Google, Bing: which ones are browsers and which are search engines? Kip and Bub sort it out, explain what a web address is, and share a tip for spotting ads in search results.

scenes.say: Is Google a browser? Is Chrome a search engine? If you're not sure, you're in good company.
Today on Tech from Scratch: browsers and search engines.
A browser is an app for visiting websites. It's the window you look through. Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Firefox are all browsers.
A search engine is a website that helps you find other websites. You type a question, and it gives you a list of results. Google, Bing, and DuckDuckGo are search engines.
Think of a library. The browser is the building you walk into. The search engine is the librarian who helps you find the right book. You use the browser to reach the search engine.
The mix-up makes sense, because Google makes a search engine and a browser. Google Search is the search engine. Chrome is the browser.

card.text: Chrome is the browser. Google is the search engine.

scenes.say: Every website also has its own address, like a street address. If you already know it, you can type it straight into the bar at the top of the browser and skip the search.
One tip. The first few search results are often ads, marked Sponsored. They can look just like real results, so take a second look before you click.
The browser is the window. The search engine is the librarian. The address takes you straight there. Next time: what is the cloud, really? Subscribe so you don't miss it.

shorts.hook: Spot the ads in your search results
